title: Understanding the Problem
text: To solve this problem, we need to determine how many turns the grindstone makes before it stops. We will use the work-energy theorem, which relates the work done by friction to the change in rotational kinetic energy.

title: Calculate the Moment of Inertia
text: The moment of inertia \( I \) for a uniform cylindrical object is calculated using the formula \( I $$=$$ \frac{1}{2} M $$R^2$$ \).

title: Moment of Inertia Calculation
text: Calculate the moment of inertia using the formula $$I=(1/2)MR**{2}$$.

title: Determine the Frictional Torque
text: The frictional force ($$F_{\text{friction}}$$) is given by $$F_{\text{friction}}$$=coefficient_of_friction*normal_force. $$The$$ $$torque$$ $$\tau$$ due to this frictional force is $$\tau=F_{\text{friction}}*R$$.

title: Apply the Work-Energy Theorem
text: The work done by the frictional torque is equal to the change in rotational kinetic energy. Use the formula: work=$$\tau*\theta$$, where $$\theta$$ is the angular displacement in radians.

title: Calculate Angular Displacement
text: Use the work-energy theorem to find $$\theta$$: work=$$\tau*\theta$$. $$The$$ $$initial$$ $$kinetic$$ $$energy$$ $$is$$ (1/2)*I*$$\omega$$**2, $$where$$ $$\omega$$ is the initial angular velocity.
